## food_menu_poster

> Vertical restaurant menu wall poster — categorized dish list with prices and accent.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1088x1920`, aspect `9:16`
**Demo vars:** `templates/food/_vars_examples/food_menu_poster.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A vertical wall-mount menu poster for Pomelo & Pine Kitchen. The poster is conceived as a single large printed sheet that diners read from across the room: a strong masthead at the top, a dish list of three featured items in the middle (Charred leek tartine, smoked ricotta — 14, Saffron orzo, blistered tomato, basil — 18, Brown-butter pear tart, creme fraiche — 9), and a quiet footer band at the bottom for hours and house notes. No food photographs, no decorative illustration.
[2. Action] The poster is purely typographic and static. The reader's eye starts at the masthead, scans down the dish stack, lingers on each dish name and price pair, and resolves at the small footer. Each dish line includes a name, a one-line ingredient note, and a price set flush right.
[3. Scene] The poster sits as a printed artifact on textured paper stock — warm cream, oat, or stone. There is no implied physical location, no restaurant interior visible behind it, no props. The background is a single calm paper tone with subtle grain.
[4. Composition] Vertical 9:16 frame. Header zone (~16%) holds the restaurant wordmark large with tight tracking. Body zone (~70%) holds the three dish blocks evenly spaced top to bottom, each set with the dish name in a display weight, the ingredient note in italic body, and the price right-aligned. Footer zone (~10%) holds a single quiet hours-and-address line. Generous outer margins of approximately 6%.
[5. Style] Independent-restaurant menu aesthetic — somewhere between a French bistro chalkboard and a Tokyo coffee-stand printed menu. Type system mixes a confident editorial serif for dish names, a humanist italic for ingredient notes, and a small caps sans for prices and the masthead. Palette is paper, warm ink, and a single accent of warm terracotta red reserved for separators and small flourishes. No food photography, no clip-art icons.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- restaurant_name: "Pomelo & Pine Kitchen"
- dish1: "Charred leek tartine, smoked ricotta — 14"
- dish2: "Saffron orzo, blistered tomato, basil — 18"
- dish3: "Brown-butter pear tart, creme fraiche — 9"

NO: real famous restaurant brand names, copyrighted franchise marks, photographic dish images, HDR oversaturation, rainbow palette, lens flare, watermarks, clip-art food icons, 3D rendered surfaces, cluttered decorative borders, cinematic teal-orange grading, busy patterned backdrops
```

## food_packaging_label

> Packaged-goods label mock — branded coffee bag, bottle, or jar wrapper design.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1152x1536`, aspect `3:4`
**Demo vars:** `templates/food/_vars_examples/food_packaging_label.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A flat front-facing packaged-goods label for Northwind Roastery, designed for the Single-Origin Filter product line in the Ethiopia Guji, washed, bergamot and stone fruit variant. The label is rendered as a single rectangular print plate, as it would appear when peeled off the package and laid flat. Typography leads; any illustrative element is small and supportive.
[2. Action] The label is a still graphic. Reader scans the brand wordmark at the top, drops into the product-line designation in the middle, notes the flavor descriptor as a smaller cross-line, and registers the weight or volume marker at the bottom. The graphic hierarchy must work at a thumbnail and at full size.
[3. Scene] The label sits flat against a calm neutral surface — recycled kraft, off-white paperboard, or pale ceramic. No physical product (no bag, no bottle, no jar) is depicted; this is the unwrapped print plate alone. Soft even daylight with no theatrical shadow.
[4. Composition] Vertical 3:4 plate. Top zone (~30%) holds the brand wordmark centered, set large with tight tracking, and a small tag line. Middle zone (~40%) holds the product-line name in display weight and the flavor descriptor as a smaller cross-line beneath it. Lower zone (~22%) holds a single small illustrative ornament (a leaf, a wave, a geometric mark) — restrained, not decorative. Footer band (~8%) holds the weight or volume in small caps.
[5. Style] Indie specialty-food packaging aesthetic — third-wave coffee roaster meets craft kombucha brewer. Type system: a confident geometric sans for the brand wordmark, an editorial serif for the product-line name, and a small caps grotesk for the weight line. Palette: a single warm paper ground, deep ink, and one saturated accent color tied to the flavor. No photographic fruit images, no metallic foiling beyond a single hairline rule.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- brand_name: "Northwind Roastery"
- product_line: "Single-Origin Filter"
- weight_volume: "250 g / 8.8 oz whole bean"

NO: real famous brand logos, copyrighted house monograms, photographic fruit imagery, HDR oversaturation, rainbow palette, lens flare, watermarks, clip-art icons, 3D rendered glossy plastic, skeuomorphic foil shimmer, cluttered decorative borders, cinematic teal-orange grading
```

## food_recipe_card

> Single-recipe card — image hero with recipe meta and key-ingredient callout.

**Artifact:** `infographic`, `1024x1280`, aspect `4:5`
**Demo vars:** `templates/food/_vars_examples/food_recipe_card.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A vertical single-recipe card for Saffron Orzo with Blistered Tomato, a Mediterranean coastal dish. The card pairs a stylized illustrated dish hero in the upper half with a typographic recipe-meta block in the lower half: dish name, prep-time label, serves label, and a single key-ingredient callout pulled forward.
[2. Action] The card is a static layout. The reader scans the dish hero illustration first, drops into the dish-name title beneath it, reads the prep-time and serves chips on the same line, and finishes on the key-ingredient callout. No step-by-step list, no nutritional breakdown — this is a hero card, not a procedural page.
[3. Scene] The card sits on a calm cream paper ground with subtle grain. The illustrated hero shows the finished dish from a soft three- quarter angle on a single ceramic plate, no garnish flourish, no styled tablescape. No physical kitchen, no hands, no props beyond the plate.
[4. Composition] Vertical 4:5 card. Hero zone (~52%) at the top holds the illustrated dish on a calm background, framed by a hairline rule. Title zone (~12%) holds the dish name in display serif weight. Meta-line zone (~10%) sits below as two pill-shaped chips: a prep-time chip on the left, a serves chip on the right. Callout zone (~16%) at the bottom holds the key-ingredient callout in italic body. Footer margin (~10%) is left clean.
[5. Style] Cookbook editorial aesthetic — a contemporary illustrated recipe page, somewhere between a Phaidon hardcover and a Sunday magazine recipe column. Illustration style: gouache-soft food rendering with honest color and gentle shadow, NOT photographic. Type system: an editorial serif for dish name and callout, a humanist sans for the meta chips. Palette: paper, ink, and the natural colors of the dish itself.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- dish_name: "Saffron Orzo with Blistered Tomato"
- prep_time_label: "Prep 35 min"
- serves_label: "Serves 4"
- key_ingredient: "Star: saffron threads, lightly bloomed in warm broth"

NO: real famous restaurant brand names, copyrighted cookbook house marks, photographic dish images, HDR oversaturation, rainbow palette, lens flare, watermarks, clip-art food icons, 3D rendered glossy plastic, cluttered decorative borders, cinematic teal-orange grading, busy patterned backdrops
```
